memories.text: I've been renting a tiny flat in Lisbon since 2021, and honestly the tram noise is the only downside.
Work-wise I'm at Brightline Analytics, mostly building dashboards for the retail team, and it pays the bills.
For context, my day job is data analysis: SQL, forecasting, and a lot of explaining charts to managers.
My usual order is black coffee with no sugar, and I get through about four a day.
When you explain things to me, keep it short and use bullet points; long paragraphs lose me.
Just so you know, I'm not allergic to peanuts; that's my brother, so satay is fine for me.
My brother Arjun lives in Leeds and we video call most Sundays.
Our team retro happens on Fridays at 4pm, which kills my weekend mood a bit.
My month-end routine: export the ledger from the finance portal, reconcile it against the warehouse numbers, then email the variance sheet to the controller before noon.
At work I've been put on the Atlas project, a pricing dashboard for one of our biggest clients.
Atlas update: we're still in the planning phase, mostly gathering requirements from the client.
I signed up with the Tagus Rowing Club for Saturday morning sessions, even though I'm terrible at it.
Just got back from a long weekend hiking on Madeira; the levada walks were stunning.
Shellfish is the one thing I really can't eat, I break out in hives within minutes.
For sourdough I feed the starter at night, mix at 7am, do four stretch-and-folds an hour apart, and bake at 250 degrees in the Dutch oven.
Correction on the retro: it moved to Thursdays at 3, and Fridays are now no-meeting days.
My sister's wedding is set for September in Goa, so I'm saving up for flights.
Atlas is owned by Northwind Retail, so every change needs their sign-off first.
Atlas is blocked right now because we still don't have access to the sales data.
Went to see Mariza live at the Coliseu last night and cried twice.
Update on my sister's wedding: they pushed it to October because of the monsoon.
The rescue dog we adopted is settling in, though she still steals socks from the laundry.
I don't own a car and honestly don't miss it; the metro covers everything I need.
Remind me to renew my residence card before the 15th of January.
Big news from my side: we finally moved to Porto in March, and the new place has a balcony over the river.
Starting in June I switched jobs and joined Tidewater Labs as a senior analyst, which still feels unreal.
Tidewater Labs is headquartered in Rotterdam, so expect a few trips to the Netherlands each quarter.
My new manager is Dana Whitlock, who is very direct but kind about feedback.
Dana works remotely from Berlin and flies in for the quarterly planning week.
I signed up for the Porto half marathon in November, which is either brave or stupid.
The doctor told me to cut back, so these days I've switched to an oat flat white once a day.
Atlas finally launched last week and the client already asked for a mobile version.
Spent a week in Copenhagen for a conference and somehow it only rained once.
Finished the Porto half marathon in 1:58, and my knees are still complaining about it.
Before a long ride I always check tyre pressure, lube the chain, and pack two spare tubes in the saddle bag.
Funny enough I've never been to Japan, even though it's at the top of my list.
Lately I've had fado playing nonstop while I work, especially the older recordings.
Need to book a dental cleaning before the end of August.
